articles.title: GTA 5 And Red Dead Redemption 2 Are Leaving PS Plus, But You Still Have Time
articles.summary: While a whole bunch of new games are being added to the PlayStation Plus Game Catalog this month, it looks like Sony is making room for them by removing several titles over the next few weeks.
body: We've known for a while that GTA 5 was on its way out, but it looks like Rockstar and Take-Two Interactive are making sure there are no distractions for the November 19 launch of GTA 6. It's worth noting that both games have been in and out of the PS Plus Game Catalog, so they'll probably be added back at some point in the future. GTA 5 rotated back into the library in November 2025, while Red Dead Redemption 2 returned to the PS Plus Extra and Premium Game Catalog in May.

Those are the biggest upcoming exits of the month, and the next noteworthy game packing its bags is The Talos Principle 2. A head-scratcher of an adventure, it's a great option for anyone looking to test their cerebral muscles while facing several existential crises about the nature of the human condition. Rock of Ages 3: Make & Break is also a recommended last-minute game to check out, as it combines tower-defense fun with quirky animations. Do you like Terry Gilliam's Monty Python cartoons? Then you'll get a kick out of this.

articles.title: Modern Warfare 4 Rescues The Reboot Series By Replicating Call of Duty’s Greatest Era
articles.summary: Modern Warfare 4's great campaign is a fun rethink of COD's finest hour, turning Modern Warfare 2's iconic moments into exciting new missions.
body: This is an IGN opinion piece from Matt Purslow, who has been playing campaign shooters since he was old enough to master WASD+mouse. He has completed every Call of Duty campaign at least once.
Warning: this article features some minor spoilers for Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4.

We’re in the final months of the year, so it’s time for the annual coin flip: is the latest Call of Duty campaign one of the good ones? The FPS series struggles with a curse few others do, zig-zagging between highs and lows, its annual cadence only making this undulating quality all the more prominent. In the last three years alone we’ve had one of its best campaigns sandwiched between two of its very worst. Thankfully, that on/off nature continues in 2026, which means it's a good year for Call of Duty. Modern Warfare 4’s campaign is one of the series’ best, and much of that is down to the fact that it replicates the formula of one of the greatest shooter campaigns ever made.

articles.title: Justice Is Keeping The GTA 6 Hype At Arm’s Length While Making Its Soundtrack
articles.summary: Grand Theft Auto 6 doesn't just look visually impressive; it also has a killer sound thanks to French electronic music duo Justice. Composing the soundtrack for any game is no easy feat, but with GTA 6 generating an unprecedented amount of hype, the team of Gaspard Augé and Xavier de Rosnay are…
body: "Yeah, we are aware of the hype of the game, of course, and the fact that people have been waiting for such a long time," Augé said in an interview with the BBC 1 radio show (via NINE1NINE ). "On the other hand, we are aware, and we see this colossus approaching, and at the same time we see it a bit from the outside. So it was a good way for us also not to let these thoughts come into our minds and not intrude on our minds."

As for the overall sound of GTA 6'S soundtrack, Justice says that it pulled from various sources to create a unique "flavor" built around several instruments. While there's a subtle '80s influence in what has been heard so far, Justice says that there's far more to the score than just retro vibes.

"We never really put words on it. 'Oh, we need to make an '80s track,' Augé said. "We knew what we needed to do, and it happened to have this kind of flavor. But at the same time, the sounds are futuristic. Like the guitar, it's not even a guitar; it's a synth, because no guitar could have this type of sound that is very phasey and a bit futuristic."
points: Grand Theft Auto 6 doesn't just look visually impressive; it also has a killer sound thanks to French electronic music duo Justice.

articles.title: Potential Steam Deck 2 Chip Shows Up in Leaked Benchmarks, Yet Another Potential Final Fantasy-Themed Codename
articles.summary: We've known for a while that Valve is working on a Steam Deck 2, but it's waiting for a chip that'll provide a "true next-generation" experience. Now, though, a potential APU for the handheld has appeared online, sparking speculation that work is ramping up.
body: The benchmark was posted on OpenBenchmarking, and shows an AMD APU codenamed 'Gainsborough,' with 6 cores and 12 threads, along with 24GB of LPDDR5 memory. However, while the the CPU side of the leaked chip is much more powerful, with 50% more cores, there is no information about the GPU, with even the graphics architecture remaining a mystery.

It's not the first time that the Gainsborough chip has appeared online. Earlier this month, Moore's Law is Dead spotted import documents for the chip, using the same 'GBR' abbreviation as the leaked AMD engineering sample. It is possible that this won't be the chip used in the final version of the Steam Deck 2, but the original Steam Deck APU was codenamed 'Aerith,' then the Steam Deck OLED got the 'Sephiroth' chip, so there's clearly a theme going with AMD's codenames for handheld chips.

articles.title: Nintendo Pays Homage to Original 1998 Commercial for The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time in New Remake Trailer
articles.summary: Nintendo has released a new The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake trailer that pays homage to the 1998 commercial for the N64 masterpiece — and we’ve got a comparison video showing just how close it is to the original.
body: Cast your mind back to 1998 and you might remember seeing a commercial for Ocarina of Time that had phrases like “A dark time is approaching,” “Willst thou run?” and “Have ye what it takes?” It’s an iconic advert that certainly got my teenage blood pumping at the time.

Now, Nintendo has recreated the advert in a new trailer for the Ocarina of Time remake. It features some of the same shots and even some of the same language. “Willst thou flee? Or Fight?” the trailer asks, leaning heavily on nostalgia as Link encounters Ganondorf on his horse — just as we see him do in the original trailer.

Reaction to the new trailer has been overwhelmingly positive, with warm memories of weekends spent in the glow of a CRT television successfully rekindled. “THEY DID THE TRAILER THING OMG,” one person said. “NO WAY THEY DID IT,” another added. “THY WILL PREORDER AS SOON AS THY GETS PAYDAY,” one fan joked.

There is one major difference though: Nintendo’s recreation does not include the custom-recorded version of the track "Riddle of Steel / Riders of Doom" from the 1982 film Conan the Barbarian, as the original trailer did. Music rights!

articles.title: “The Suits” Made All The Money From Call Of Duty: Black Ops 1 And 2 Ports, OG Dev Says
articles.summary: Activision recently released ports of 2010's Call of Duty: Black Ops and 2012's Call of Duty: Black Ops 2 on PlayStation, and they were massive hits. According to a report, the games combined to sell more than 11 million copies on PS4 and PS5.
body: Posting on LinkedIn, Goslin said it's amazing to see these games continue to perform well in 2026. It's also a bit sad because the "suits" at Activision are raking in all the money, not the original developers, he said.

"I poured my life into those games, spending countless, brutal hours in crunch alongside an incredibly talented team to make sure they were perfect. Seeing our blood, sweat, and tears still dominating the charts in 2026 is amazing, but it's hard to watch the suits rake in giant financial windfalls from our old code while the actual creators don't see a dime of it," he said ( via VGC ). "If executives are getting massive bonuses off the longevity of these classics, that wealth needs to be shared retroactively. Legacy revenue should mean legacy rewards for the devs who survived the crunch to build them."
As Goslin mentioned here, the re-releases are not remakes or remasters--instead, they are ports with no new features or significant updates, and that's exactly what fans had been clamoring for.

"As a developer who actually worked on both BO1 and BO2, seeing these charts is bittersweet. I poured my life into those games, spending countless, brutal hours in crunch alongside an incredibly talented team to make sure they were perfect. Seeing our blood, sweat, and tears still dominating the charts in 2026 is amazing, but it's hard to watch the suits rake in giant financial windfalls from our old code while the actual creators don't see a dime of it."

The post was subsequently picked up by various gaming websites - a recirculation Goslin reacted to in a separate post on LinkedIn today. "I am glad this critical conversation is gaining traction," Goslin said.

articles.title: This Year’s Most Underrated Fantasy Film Officially Lands on Digital Early
articles.summary: A bevy of must-watch movies came out in September, like Your Mother Your Mother Your Mother, Resident Evil, and Primetime. The animated fantasy film Forgotten Island mostly slipped through the cracks, failing to make much of a splash at the box office despite a wave of positive critical and…
body: Whether it wasn't marketed much or just had bad timing, Forgotten Island has largely come and gone from theaters unnoticed. But, starting next week, you can check out the most underrated film of the year from the comfort of your couch.

On Tuesday, Universal announced Forgotten Island will be available to rent and purchase digitally starting Oct. 27, months before it hits streaming services. Its physical editions will be released just over a month later on Dec. 1.

From writer-directors Januel Mercado and Joel Crawford, who also directed 2022's Puss in Boots: The Last Wish, Forgotten Island is about best friends Jo (H.E.R.) and Raissa (Liza Soberano) on their last night together before their lives take them in different directions. They get swept away to a mythical island filled with fantastical creatures, but can't remember the night they spent there. They then search for a way home and piece together the events of their adventure-filled night while being reminded of why their friendship is so strong.

articles.title: Disney Finally Has a Plan To Save Star Wars, but There’s a Catch
articles.summary: As Star Wars turns 50 in 2027, the galaxy-spanning franchise’s reputation feels like it’s been on a seesaw. It has scored a handful of wins, particularly with Andor’s Emmy success and the positive reception of Disney’s latest animated offering, Maul: Shadow Lord.
body: Worse still, the future of Star Wars doesn’t look particularly exciting, at least if you’re a fan only interested in what Disney and Lucasfilm have in store for Star Wars TV and film projects. Half of them seem to be on ice, and the other half plan on retreading old ground like the Skywalkers. Yawn. Barely worth talking about.
However, there is hope for Star Wars — and it rests entirely on the shoulders of Lucasfilm Games and its open-minded vision for a galaxy far, far away.

In 2013, Lucasfilm Games and Disney signed a 10-year exclusive licensing agreement that let EA publish Star Wars games, leading to standout titles like DICE’s Star Wars: Battlefront series and Respawn’s Jedi games starring Cal Kestis (Cameron Monaghan). That exclusivity ran out in 2023, allowing Lucasfilm Games to be far less restrictive with the Star Wars franchise.

In an interview with The Game Business Show, Lucasfilm Games executive Douglas Reilly discussed the success of Star Wars video games and how that success came from being “more flexible” about who Lucasfilm Games is willing to take pitches from. “Good ideas,” Reilly explained, “can come from a lot of different places.”

articles.title: Helldivers 2 swaps over to Easy anti-cheat, with developers admitting Gameguard "wasn't as effective as it could have been"
articles.summary: Helldivers will be switching up its anti-cheat, as developer Arrowhead Game Studios has admitted that its Gameguard cheat policy "wasn't as effective as it could have been."
body: As part of this shift, Arrowhead also confirmed that several non-malicious mods, such as cosmetic changes, will need to be updated to work alongside Easy Anti-Cheat. "We know mods are part of the DNA of PC gaming and gaming communities as a whole. In general, we appreciate the creativity behind cosmetic and non-gameplay mods, which players can enjoy without negatively impacting those who play alongside them," the post reads.

"Where we need to improve is how we protect players against modifications that create unfair advantages or negatively impact others, which goes beyond software manipulation to tamper with our game. These changes mean that some mods, particularly the types that are affecting the experience of other players, may no longer function."

The post continues to implore those who feel a non-malicious mod has been blocked by Easy Anti-Cheat to reach out via Zendesk. So, there should be a bit of a rough transitional period, but hopefully a lot of the fun mods should be good to go again in the near future.

articles.title: God of War Creator Reveals Why Kratos’ Original Name Was Abandoned
articles.summary: It seems that Kratos was almost the god of a very different realm: pizza. God of War creator David Jaffe revealed on X that Kratos was originally named Dominus, until a relentless onslaught of Domino’s Pizza jokes made him reconsider.
body: “Dominus sounded brutal, and violent, and dominant,” Jaffe said. “I just loved that name. I thought it was great. But then something started happening at the studio. The people on the team started making Domino’s Pizza jokes. Every single time someone said Dominus, someone inevitably would yell out ’30 minutes or free’ or ‘Get the door, it’s Dominus,’ or talk about the f**ng Noid. After about the 50th time, the writing was on the wall. Dominus was dead.” It’s worth noting that Dominus isn’t a Greek name, but a Roman one derived from the Latin word for “lord” or “master.”

Jaffe went on to explain that someone printed out a massive list of ancient Greek male baby names for him to sort through, but none of the ones he picked stuck. At this point, the game’s marketing lead, Susan Panico, pitched the name Kratos, which resonated with the team. Jaffe later realized that Kratos was on the original list of names, but that he had missed it entirely. “I guess it goes to show you how much of success in games is just luck and timing, and in this case, marketing.” In Ancient Greek, kratos means "power" or "strength," so it was a pretty apt name for the protagonist.
points: It seems that Kratos was almost the god of a very different realm: pizza.

articles.title: People who've finished Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 on the new YOLO, single-life difficulty share experiences and tips for doing so
articles.summary: The Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 campaign is currently available in early access, and if you're among the many who pre-ordered a copy in order to play it before launch, you've likely noticed a locked difficulty setting that's harder, even, than Realism.
body: YOLO, which is short for you only live once, is a new difficulty tier introduced in Modern Warfare 4. It does exactly what you expect: gives you a single life to complete the entirety of the campaign. Die once and you're sent back to the start.
A few players have already cleared the Modern Warfare 4 campaign on YOLO, but one in particular took the time to answer a few questions and reveal some of their toughest moments in the campaign.

Reddit user Lost-Equivalent2352 shared a screenshot showing a completed campaign at YOLO difficulty, which they said took them 20 hours. Key to their strategy was, well, a lot of hiding and leaving AI teammates to kill as many enemies as possible, before emerging to finish the rest. They relied on flashbangs to momentarily stun enemies and make it easier to shoot them, but they also used a lot of grenades to clear clusters of enemies.

videos.title: Final Fantasy Resonance Video Review
videos.summary: Final Fantasy Resonance reviewed by Michael Higham on Nintendo Switch 2.
body: "Part of playing through Final Fantasy Resonance is to examine why an older era of RPG was wedged into our psyche for so long. The rose-tinted glasses can be strong at times, but so too was the sharpness of their messages, and the ones we remember most fondly understood that simple did not mean shallow. And that's the biggest thing Resonance couldn't really nail down. Even with weaker dialogue that fills large stretches of its story, the journey is still worth embarking on. Resonance is special for how it wields HD-2D as an art style to set a new, higher standard that goes well beyond nostalgia. It's the flair that makes a solid turn-based combat system more satisfying when beating down a staggered boss. And it's what paints its world as an exciting place to explore, especially when a superb soundtrack backs up each moment before hitting you with a nasty battle theme. Although I'm left underwhelmed by pieces of the storytelling itself, I'm glad Final Fantasy Resonance exists to revive Brave Exvius but also show that old-school style RPGs can keep raising the bar in more ways than one."

videos.title: Dragon’s Dogma 2: Dark Arisen Review
videos.summary: Dragon’s Dogma 2: Dark Arisen reviewed by Jarrett Green on PlayStation 5, also available on Xbox, PC, and Nintendo Switch 2.
body: "Dragon’s Dogma 2: Dark Arisen’s avalanche of new content is an icy salve for the burns left by a modern world full of incremental live-service updates. Trudging through the oppressive snowdrifts of this charming new region for dozens of hours felt like uncovering a past where games dropped meaty, activity-filled expansions all the time – fitting for a game so spiritually linked to a version of itself from 14 years ago. It's not all divine, as the campaign spends far too much of its final moments driving on repetitive tasks and its new Spoils slot machine makes the endgame gear hunt more lifeless than the frozen wastes you scrounge them from. But the journey, full of new and interesting characters, vibrant and violent enemies, and the wonderful wreckage of a bygone civilization, is an engrossing adventure worth the investment."
points: Dragon’s Dogma 2: Dark Arisen reviewed by Jarrett Green on PlayStation 5, also available on Xbox, PC, and Nintendo Switch 2.
"Dragon’s Dogma 2: Dark Arisen’s avalanche of new content is an icy salve for the burns left by a modern world full of incremental live-service updates.

Trudging through the oppressive snowdrifts of this charming new region for dozens of hours felt like uncovering a past where games dropped meaty, activity-filled expansions all the time – fitting for…
But the journey, full of new and interesting characters, vibrant and violent enemies, and the wonderful wreckage of a bygone civilization, is an engrossing adventure worth the investment."
